MorphoHand · real_v1 fingertip and screwdriver, two-pad rig · contact comparison bed · 5 October 2026 · built 2026-10-05 14:17

Agreement and cost of five fingertip contact models on pinch, twist, roll, shake and brake tasks

The 1 mm sphere pad spins the screwdriver at 6 % less torque than Drake hydroelastic from 0.5 to 3 N, slips at the same pull force, and brakes the swing to within 1° of Drake. condim 4 with its torsional coefficient rescheduled is within 6 % of the torque but has a single contact point. Point contact transmits no torque, and the tool swings through. Newton hydroelastic, now stable at 1 ms, starts to spin at 2.3–2.5× the law’s torque, the largest disagreement in the bed. Under a held load below the slip force, every MuJoCo model creeps (slides slowly) about 100× faster than Drake. The pad costs 13–24 µs per step against 1–2 ms for Drake and 0.5–3 ms for Newton on one GPU world. Roll, creep and the stability map were cut off and are listed at the end with their scripts.

Terms and metrics

pad
One fingertip’s contact with the tool. On the bed rig two pads, one per fingertip, pinch the tool; N is the normal force of each pad.
friction arm
Pressure-weighted mean distance of the contact patch from its centre, (1), in mm. A pad transmits at most about its normal before it spins. The hydroelastic law gives 0.84, 1.00 and 1.31 mm at 0.5, 1 and 3 N.
slip onset, effective μ
Task 1 raises an axial force on the tool at 2 N/s. Before onset the tool slides slowly at a speed proportional to the force; onset is the force at which the speed leaves that trend. Effective μ is the onset force divided by 2N (two pads). Rigid Coulomb friction gives 1.000.
creep
Steady sliding of the tool while the load stays below the slip force. Task 1 holds the axial force at half the onset force for 1 s and reports the sliding speed in µm/s; task 2 holds half the onset torque and reports the turning speed in °/s; in task 4 it is the drift per cycle below the Coulomb threshold. Rigid Coulomb friction gives zero.
slip speed
Mean sliding speed of the tool over the 50 ms after onset in task 1, in mm/s. Rigid Coulomb friction with equal static and kinetic μ gives 34 mm/s.
arm at spin onset
Task 2 raises a torque about the pinch axis; the onset torque divided by 2μN, in mm per pad. Sliding arm: the steady torque while the tool is driven to spin at 1 rad/s, divided by 2μN. Onset / law: onset torque over the hydroelastic law’s 2μN·cN1/4.
drift per cycle
Net displacement of the tool along its axis per 5 Hz shake cycle in task 4. Coulomb load ratio: m(g + apk)/(2μN); rigid Coulomb friction slips above 1.
swing end, peak rate
Task 5 lowers the pinch force until the tool swings about the pinch axis. Swing end is the final angle (90° = hanging); peak rate the largest angular speed of the swing, in °/s.
physics step Δt
The simulator’s integration step; 1 ms unless stated. µs per step: wall time of one physics step on one CPU core, controller and rendering excluded. World-steps per second: on the GPU, the number of parallel simulations times the steps each completes per second.
tc, d0, Λ̂
MuJoCo contact parameters. tc, the solref time constant, sets how fast a penetration is corrected; d0, the solimp impedance, sets what fraction of that correction the solver enforces; Λ̂ is MuJoCo’s estimate of the contact’s inverse inertia (47.2 kg−1 for a pad on the real tool). Together they set the sphere stiffness, (10).
impratio, condim
impratio: ratio of friction-row to normal-row stiffness in MuJoCo; larger values make friction stick harder. condim 3: normal force and two friction directions; condim 4 adds torsional friction about the normal.
pad spacing
Distance between neighbouring sphere centres on a sphere pad. The 2, 1 and 0.5 mm pads have 51, 205 and 819 spheres on a 45° cap.
relaxation time tr
Drake’s dissipation time for hydroelastic contact; the pads use tc = tr/2 so both damp at the same rate.

Rig, models and protocol

Every case runs on the two-pad pinch rig of the 10-01 study (scripts/hom_contact_rig.py): two real_v1 fingertip spheres on rails along x press the screwdriver, whose axis lies along y, with a commanded force N per pad. Tasks add one load or motion each. The protocol (docs/experiments/20261005-contact_bed/PROTOCOL.md) fixes the parameters, metrics and row fields for every script, so rows written by different scripts and simulators compare directly. 177 rows so far. Task 1: pull to slip

Protocol: the pinch settles at N for 0.4 s, then an axial force on the tool rises at 2 N/s until the tool slides faster than 10 mm/s. A second run holds the force at half the onset force for 1 s to measure creep.

Task 2: twist to spin

Protocol: after settling, a torque about the pinch axis rises at the law’s torque per second until the tool turns faster than 30 °/s. A second run holds half the onset torque for 1 s to measure creep, and a third drives the tool to spin at 1 rad/s to measure the sliding arm.

Table: task 2 at a 1 ms step. The law is the hydroelastic arm fitted to Drake on this rig, 0.996 mm·N−1/4. Point contact has no torsional friction; its onset value is the torque at which its creep reached the detection speed.

Newton hydroelastic starts to spin at 2.3–2.9× the law’s torque with and without contact reduction, and its 5 ms runs spin at once or eject the tool. Its static pinch on the same rig has the expected normal force, so the excess is in the friction it applies across the patch. The probe’s friction gain (kf10 in the spec) and the 100× stiffer tool are the first two settings to vary.

Task 6: creep, impratio and noslip

Task 6 (creep) was not run: scripts/contact_bed_creep.py is written; its launches were refused by the memory guard while swap stood above 15 GB, then the session limit stopped the agent.

Task 7: largest stable step

Task 7 (stability map) was not run: scripts/contact_bed_stability.py is written. The bound it tests is equation (14) of the overview page; Codex’s step sweep and the load-time calibration study already bracket it at two points (the 4× tool holds at 2.5 ms and fails at 3 ms against d0tc = 2.65 ms).

Consistency of the pads

The 1 mm pad gives the same task results from 0.5 to 5 ms steps: the arm at onset moves by under 1 % and the swing end by under 0.1°. The 0.5 mm pad agrees with it; the 2 mm pad touches with too few spheres at 0.5 N, and its arm there is less than half the law’s.

What this does not settle

  • Roll, creep and the stability map. Run scripts/contact_bed_roll.py, scripts/contact_bed_creep.py and scripts/contact_bed_stability.py (written, not run; each resumes from its JSONL).
  • Newton’s torsion. Repeat task 2 in Newton with the friction gain at 1 and the tool at the pad’s stiffness; an arm near the law would locate the 2.4–2.9× excess in those settings.
  • Newton on the GPU. Its throughput rows stop at 1024 worlds unreduced and 4096 reduced; finish 4096–8192 with scripts/newton_scaling.py once task 2 agrees, so that the throughput comparison is between models that agree in torsion.
  • CPU against GPU pads. scripts/pads_cpu_gpu_consistency.py wrote three CPU rows; the MuJoCo-Warp twins decide whether the GPU throughput describes the same physics.
  • Creep. Every MuJoCo model creeps about 100× faster than Drake under a held load; task 6 tests impratio 1000 and noslip_iterations 10.
